Vanessa —

Thanks for the MAP and the eval spreadsheet. Monday 6/7 at 11am ET works for us. For the kickoff, here are the technical priorities from our side so we can be efficient:
1) Auth: We use short-lived JWTs issued by our Identity service; need to confirm if Redwood SDK can accept our token format or if we should implement a token-exchange proxy.
2) Streaming: Target is <200ms tail latency for enriched event payloads when operating at expected steady-state (approx 5k events/day).
3) Tool calling: Our playbook runner expects a JSON-RPC-like callback and idempotent operations. Can the Redwood tool-call interface guarantee at-least-once delivery and request dedup keys?

I'll invite our tech lead (Priya) and security contact to the kickoff. Also, please confirm if there is a standard NDA/PO required before we exchange any production test data — we can fast-track that if needed.

Best,

Alex —

Appreciate the clear priorities. Quick technical response and attached checklist (NN_EvalSpec_v0.3.xlsx contains the actionable test cases):

1) Auth: Redwood SDK supports bearer tokens in the Authorization header. We can accept Nimbus JWTs directly if the token includes standard claims (iss, sub, exp) and is signed with an accepted algorithm. If Nimbus requires a token-exchange pattern (OIDC token broker), we can support a lightweight proxy — estimate 3-5 dev-days for a minimal token-exchange service and 1-2 days of SE configuration. Action: Rafael to produce short options doc by 2027-06-09.

2) Streaming: Our hosted demo can run initial latency captures but for a realistic warm-cache tail-latency test we recommend a dedicated sandbox GPU node so we can reproduce steady-state KV-cache behavior. Estimated cost and time to spin up: 2 business days. Monica, can you confirm whether Nimbus will provision test event samples or will we synthesize?

3) Tool-calling: Redwood tool-call interface guarantees at-least-once delivery and supports idempotency keys passed via the tool invocation metadata. We surface retry headers so your runner can detect duplicates. We also have a small deterministic replay harness in the eval spreadsheet for validating idempotent behavior.

Next steps / short list for the kickoff:
- Rafael: options doc for auth (due 6/9) [attached summary]
- Monica: sandbox decision + test dataset confirmation (due 6/11)
- Vanessa: procurement/NDA status and purchase order path

Attachments: NN_EvalSpec_v0.3.xlsx (test cases and replay harness), MAP_Nimbus_v1.pdf

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
